races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Molo Del Palazzo
runners_data.note: True hold-up type trained by Ralph Beckett who has shown no wins or placed efforts in this combination of style and trip; 23 days since last run is fine but the 1m2f with a controlled pace may not generate enough of a true run to bring him into contention from the rear.

runners_data.name: Blue Noon
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner whose Unknown style is an interesting X-factor at 1m2f; three consecutive 10f runs on Good ground with a placed effort suggests the trip suits, though the modest pace map gives little incentive for a horse needing strong fractions to build momentum.

runners_data.name: Tai Hang Pegasus
runners_data.note: 132 days off the track is the headline concern for Pat Cosgrave and Charlie Fellowes; placed twice at 8-9f on Soft but the step to 1m2f Good after a long break on a trainer with just 1 win from 3 in the last 14 days adds layers of uncertainty despite solid benchmark form.

runners_data.name: Mostaan
runners_data.note: Unknown style for Owen Burrows, who is 2/11 in the past fortnight — a quiet spell; two runs on Standard going without a win or place hint he struggles to land a blow when the pace is steady and the field compact over this sort of trip.

runners_data.name: Light Dreamer
runners_data.note: Holds a placed effort on Standard going (2nd at 7f) and shaped with promise when second at 8f on Good; Joe Leavy keeps it simple from midfield and this horse could be the most interesting mid-division threat if the pace compresses toward home.

runners_data.name: Windbreaker
runners_data.note: William Haggas, 12 wins from 47 in 14 days, saddles this Unknown-style runner who has placed at both 8f and 10f — including a third at 10f Soft suggesting stamina holds; 28 days since last run is normal and Darragh Keenan can position where needed.

runners_data.name: Last Verse
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator whose natural position is toward the rear but is mapped to midfield due to congestion at the back — 289 days off the track is a significant flag, and Andrew Balding would likely want a confidence-building run here before expecting a bold showing; discount accordingly.

runners_data.name: Alice De Clare
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the field and, with back-to-back wins at 10f Good ground, she carries clear course-and-distance form; George Wood can set his own fractions and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects she may be pressed more than ideal, but her record makes her the pivotal pace asset in this race.

runners_data.name: Oh Yes You Do
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's prominent runner has won at 8f Soft and placed at 10f Good — the trip profile fits — and Dylan Hogan is likely to push forward to track Alice De Clare; the 31 days since last run is unremarkable and a clear run in second could set this horse up well for a straight-line challenge.

runners_data.name: Antiquarian
runners_data.note: Gary & Moore's hold-up type has been slotted into midfield because the rear is crowded — but his true inclination is to race from the back; 14 days since last run is the shortest turnaround in the field, form shows a 10th on Standard going last time, and the 7lb claim for Jude Fernandes does not offset the positional compromise and weak recent figures.

races.paceDynamic: Alice De Clare is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with only Oh Yes You Do likely to press from a prominent position, she faces no serious early challenge and should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f Good-ground trip. That uncontested lead creates a rail-hugging, even-tempo race where the early sectionals will be measured rather than pressured, handing Alice De Clare a significant positional advantage heading into the home straight. The field holds more true hold-up types than can be accommodated at the rear — Last Verse and Antiquarian are genuine closers mapped forward into midfield because there simply is not room for all of them to find their natural position; Alice De Clare and Oh Yes You Do are most likely to actually secure the front two slots. This race shape most clearly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the tempo and pounce in the straight without having to make up significant ground from off the pace.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Alice De Clare dictates an uncontested, even pace and the race develops into a straight-line stamina test.
scenarios.body: If Alice De Clare dictates an uncontested, even pace and the race develops into a straight-line stamina test.

scenarios.trigger: If Alice De Clare bowls along at only a modest clip and energy-conserving midfield runners produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: If Alice De Clare bowls along at only a modest clip and energy-conserving midfield runners produce a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong and the front two tie each other up, leaving a gap for back-of-field runners to close.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves deceptively strong and the front two tie each other up, leaving a gap for back-of-field runners to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexposed Types Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If the step up in trip unlocks a three-year-old who has been underperforming at shorter distances, producing a surprise winner.
scenarios.body: If the step up in trip unlocks a three-year-old who has been underperforming at shorter distances, producing a surprise winner.

watchPoints.text: Alice De Clare holds the pace key to this race — if George Wood gets a clean break and settles into a rhythm unchallenged, she could prove very difficult to run down given her back-to-back 10f Good-ground wins.

Oh Yes You Do is most likely to track Alice De Clare and apply gentle pressure; if Dylan Hogan pushes forward early and the two establish a lead gap, the hold-up horses mapped to midfield face a near-impossible task bridging it late.

Last Verse's 289-day absence makes her a major fitness unknown — her redistribution from natural hold-up to mapped midfield compounds the risk, and any sign of her being slowly away or missing the break should be noted as a race-defining moment for the rear-of-field scenario.

Light Dreamer showed a placed effort on Standard going at 7f and a second at 8f Good — if she settles mid-group early and the pace proves genuinely even, she represents the most credible non-prominent challenge worth monitoring from the home turn.

Tai Hang Pegasus returns from 132 days off for a trainer with just 1 win from 3 recently; watch for signs in the pre-race canter and early strides whether Charlie Fellowes has her race-fit, as a stiff task first time back over this trip on Good ground could quickly expose any fitness deficit.

races.name: Sandy Is Going The Distance At 80 Classified Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Belle Of Kt
runners_data.note: Strong course and distance form with 1W6P on similar going across 10 runs, Tony Carroll's in-form yard has been firing, and 85 days off is manageable given that fitness profile; holds up naturally but has the flexibility and the best sim-going record in the field to thrive in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Dubai Immo
runners_data.note: Tom Queally takes the ride for Paddy Butler who has had just 0/2 in the past 14 days; wears tongue-tie, has 71 days between runs, and although the horse's natural instinct is to come from the back, it has been slotted into a midfield role that asks it to race out of character — form at this trip on Standard is sketchy (1W3P from 15 runs).

runners_data.name: Harry Don't Bite
runners_data.note: Very recent run (8 days ago) is a fitness plus for Camilla Poulton's runner, but the form string of 799670 is deeply uninspiring and all five historical runs were over shorter trips (7f-8f) — stepping up to 1m2f is a significant ask; slots into midfield on the map but races genuinely from the rear, which is a further complication in a slow-run contest.

runners_data.name: Myna
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good ground recently and has shown 1W3P across nine similar-going runs, with the headgear note (h) suggesting hood could sharpen focus; William Carson is a strong booking and this horse has the distance form to be dangerous if it can secure a handy position.

runners_data.name: Pureis King
runners_data.note: The fades-in-finish flag is a meaningful concern for Faye Bramley's four-year-old who has finished 8th, 8th, and 10th in its last three outings, all at shorter trips than today; 51 days off and 0W0P on comparable going make this a tough task, though the sprint-finish scenario suits horses that can at least travel well before the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Pure Theory
runners_data.note: Apprentice Rose Dawes (5lb claim) takes the ride, but Stephanie Cassidy's horse has a concerning pattern of double-digit finishes and has gone 0W1P from 10 similar-going runs; its natural racing style is prominent despite being shown in midfield here, meaning it will struggle to get its ideal berth in this configuration.

runners_data.name: Qaaeadd
runners_data.note: Mark Usher's four-year-old has worn a tongue-tie, was last seen just 10 days ago finishing 7th, and has only four runs on Standard going yielding 0W0P; showed a respectable 5th at 1m2f on Soft last time which gives some distance encouragement, and Callum Rodriguez is an experienced pilot.

runners_data.name: Shifra
runners_data.note: Pat Phelan's runner has the fades-in-finish concern and only 2/8 runs on Good going have been placed, but there is a snippet of promise — a 2nd over 10f on Good ground lurks in the form; genuinely a hold-up performer pushed into a midfield slot that does not suit, and the step up in trip beyond 10f here is uncharted territory.

runners_data.name: Summer Evening
runners_data.note: David Flood's runner wears headgear (tp) and has shown 0W2P from 11 similar-going starts, with a recent 74-day break to factor in; naturally comes from off the pace but the map shows it in midfield, meaning Darragh Keenan will need to make a decision early about whether to commit or drop out — the 21st of 21 at Sandown over 8f on Soft last time warrants scrutiny.

runners_data.name: Henfield
runners_data.note: Karen Jewell's three-year-old carries the fades-in-finish flag and has a modest form string of 580-9 with no wins or places in those four runs; only one of those came beyond 8f so the step to 1m2f is a genuine stamina question, and being a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield in a race with zero front-runners is a difficult position.

runners_data.name: High Boltage
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's three-year-old was last seen 97 days ago and has the fades-in-finish flag alongside a tongue-tie and hood; the sim-going record shows 0W0P from four Standard runs and all five historical starts have been between 6f and 10f, so today's 1m2f represents a distance question mark on top of an already concerning profile.

runners_data.name: Ruiz
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's three-year-old carries a headgear note (h) and fades-in-finish flag, was last seen 14 days ago finishing 0th/0th in its last pair of runs, and has gone 0W0P across four Standard-going appearances; the lowest OR in the field at 40, partnered by Alec Voikhansky, and the redistribution out of its natural rear-of-field position makes this a very difficult puzzle to solve.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field, the early gallop is likely to be tentative and uncontested, drifting into a slowly-run affair before the field compresses and the race is effectively decided in a sprint finish over the final two furlongs. Belle Of Kt is the most interesting pace factor given her form at this trip and course, but she is a hold-up type herself, meaning there is genuinely nobody with a natural desire to bowl along and set a true tempo. The entire field is composed of hold-up or midfield horses, so the map is forced to redistribute runners such as Henfield, Harry Don't Bite, Summer Evening, High Boltage, Shifra, Dubai Immo, Pure Theory, and Ruiz into midfield slots they would not naturally occupy — several of these are true hold-up types who will want to race further back than the map shows, making the early-pace vacuum even more pronounced. This race shape strongly favours horses with tactical versatility to sit handy in a falsely-run contest and accelerate late, rewarding those with proven form at the distance on Good ground and a jockey willing to commit early.

scenarios.title: Crawl Then Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field drifts at a crawl through the first mile and erupts into a mass sprint over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the field drifts at a crawl through the first mile and erupts into a mass sprint over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Modest Pace, Class Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one runner edges into a narrow lead at a steady pace and the race becomes a test of sustained finishing quality.
scenarios.body: If one runner edges into a narrow lead at a steady pace and the race becomes a test of sustained finishing quality.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out and a true hold-up runner threads through traffic to land a late blow.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out and a true hold-up runner threads through traffic to land a late blow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed, sprint-style finish produces interference or multiple horses hitting the line together with little to separate them.
scenarios.body: If the compressed, sprint-style finish produces interference or multiple horses hitting the line together with little to separate them.

watchPoints.text: Belle Of Kt has the strongest combination of course-and-distance form, similar-going record (10 runs, 1W6P), and jockey profile in a race with no genuine pace — if she secures an easy position in midfield she could prove very hard to beat in a sprint finish.

The entire field is composed of hold-up types and several horses (Harry Don't Bite, Dubai Immo, Ruiz, Henfield) are genuinely out of their natural running style today — watch for a chaotic early furlong as jockeys attempt to avoid settling last, which could cause a surprisingly quick early pace despite no designated front-runner.

Myna's recent win over 10f on Good ground and the hood headgear makes it a live threat if William Carson elects to take up a prominent early position rather than hold up — a horse of this profile racing handily in a slow-run contest could be very dangerous.

High Boltage (97 days off) and Belle Of Kt (85 days off) are the two longest-absent runners — fitness at reappearance is worth monitoring in the market, though the latter's trainer form and course record suggests readiness.

Three horses carry the fades-in-finish flag (Pureis King, Shifra, Henfield, High Boltage, Ruiz) — in a compressed sprint finish these horses are at structural disadvantage and should be downgraded in any scenario where the race is truly run at a crawl and decided by finishing speed alone.

races.name: Sandy Is Going The Distance At 80 Classified Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Eager Puccini
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse with a visor background whose recent form reads 700-68 — finishing tendencies are a concern flagged by the fades-in-finish warning, and the 40-day break adds uncertainty; genuinely suited to racing from the rear but will find itself shuffled into midfield by the volume of hold-up types here.

runners_data.name: Hawaiian King
runners_data.note: Has headgear and six runs in form with one place at 10f on Standard; true racing style is from the back but the redistribution in this field means a closer position is likely, which may not play to its strengths given modest sim-going figures of 8/10 with no wins.

runners_data.name: Lady Aiyana
runners_data.note: Trainer Gansera-Leveque sends her out 16 days after her last run with a tongue-tie; she has placed at 12f on Standard and at 10f, suggesting stamina is not an issue, but as a hold-up horse forced into a midfield berth by the crowded back-end of this field, her finishing kick is dependent on pace developing ahead.

runners_data.name: Monks Mead
runners_data.note: Mark Usher has had two winners from 11 runners in the last 14 days so the yard is in form; despite being a hold-up horse by nature, Monks Mead's recent placing record at 10f on Standard (four places from 15 runs) makes it one of the more reliable outsiders, even if it will race out of its preferred position.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Cloud
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with headgear, 13 days since last run, and only one place from five recent runs on Good or Standard over 10f — the age and slim recent profile make it hard to favour, even though it races from behind which is at least consistent with the majority style in this field.

runners_data.name: Pablo Prince
runners_data.note: William Carson partners this consistent Standard specialist who has placed three times from 13 runs on that surface, all at 10-12f — the extra distance of 10f here suits a horse that has consistently placed at 12f, and as a true hold-up runner whose map position is not redistributed, the notes are genuinely authentic.

runners_data.name: Reel Power
runners_data.note: Tom Queally takes the ride on a seven-year-old wearing a visor whose sim-going record of 9/15 runs shows no wins and only one place on Good or Standard; finishing from the rear is its natural mode but the redistribution into midfield and uninspiring recent figures (498-80) make it hard to advocate.

runners_data.name: Rockafeller Skank
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer has hit 6 from 16 over 14 days in excellent form, and this three-year-old is on a three-race winning streak at 8f on Standard and Soft — the step up to 10f on Good is the main query, but the uncontested lead is a significant compensating factor and the lowest OR in the field (25) suggests assessors have yet to catch up with this run of form.

runners_data.name: Amalfi Bluebell
runners_data.note: 277 days off the track is the dominant concern for this three-year-old, and the limited form string (0577-) on good or soft ground at 6-8f doesn't inspire confidence at this longer trip on Standard; a natural hold-up runner who will be displaced from its preferred rear position by the overcrowded backfield.

runners_data.name: Pam's Sonnet
runners_data.note: Callum Hutchinson partners a three-year-old whose five recent runs are all in single-figure finishes but none in the frame — consistent midfield finishing without the killer kick, and sim-going of 4/5 runs on Standard suggests no surface concern, but the form simply doesn't show a winning profile at this level.

runners_data.name: Raise The Stakes
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes the ride but this three-year-old is flagged for fading in the finish, wears a visor, and the form string (960-09) alongside all five recent runs finishing outside the first five makes this a difficult horse to support regardless of race shape; the 16-day turnaround is fine but the finishing tendency is the overriding issue.

runners_data.name: Sir Patchy
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — flagged accordingly; a natural hold-up horse with the fades-in-finish warning and a 49-day break, whose last five runs are all on Standard at 8-13f with two places, but the non-runner status renders further analysis moot.

races.paceDynamic: Rockafeller Skank is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, having won three in a row most recently, will stride to the front unchallenged from the off, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 1m2f at Lingfield. With no rival willing or able to press for the lead, the pace is likely to be modest early, stringing the field out behind one horse rather than generating the tempo that suits closers. The absence of meaningful pace pressure means Rockafeller Skank can dictate margins, conserve energy through the bend, and ask the question on her own terms in the straight — a scenario that strongly favours the leader and any horse close enough to track without expending energy. This race shape favours prominent racers who can sit just off a gentle gallop and pounce, rather than genuine hold-up types who need pace to run into. The field contains far more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Monks Mead, Lady Aiyana, Hawaiian King, Amalfi Bluebell, Eager Puccini, Reel Power, and Sir Patchy are all natural hold-up horses who will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would choose, reducing their effectiveness as late finishers.

scenarios.body: If Rockafeller Skank breaks cleanly and settles in an uncontested lead at a pace of her own choosing.

scenarios.trigger: If Rockafeller Skank sets too slow a pace, causing the field to bunch and triggering a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If Rockafeller Skank sets too slow a pace, causing the field to bunch and triggering a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Upsides
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types secures an unusually prominent position and benefits from sitting just off the pace.
scenarios.body: If one of the redistributed hold-up types secures an unusually prominent position and benefits from sitting just off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Increases, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace hotts up mid-race or a rival challenges Rockafeller Skank, testing stamina over the 10f trip.
scenarios.body: If the pace hotts up mid-race or a rival challenges Rockafeller Skank, testing stamina over the 10f trip.

watchPoints.text: Rockafeller Skank is on a three-race winning streak and faces zero pace rivals — watch whether she builds an unassailable lead turning for home, which would leave the entire field with ground to make up in the straight.

Monks Mead is the most likely of the redistributed hold-up horses to secure a better position than its natural style suggests, given Mark Usher's yard being in 14-day form (2/11); if it tracks the leader comfortably it enters the mix.

Pablo Prince has run 13 of 15 career runs on Standard and is proven at 12f — if the pace is truly modest and the race develops into a stamina test in the final two furlongs, his consistent sim-going profile gives him each-way claims.

Amalfi Bluebell has not run for 277 days and steps up sharply in trip from 6-7f to 10f — monitor the market move; if unconsidered in the market that layoff and trip jump are likely being reflected in the price.

Sir Patchy is currently listed as a non-runner — if confirmed withdrawn the field drops to 11, which slightly loosens the congestion of hold-up types at the rear and could marginally improve the positional prospects of the remaining backmarkers.

races.name: Gatwick Kia PV5 Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Garrincha
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner from the Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill yard making his first run in 168 days, which is a significant concern; Pat Cosgrave takes the ride and the horse should lead unchallenged, but the fitness question after such a lengthy absence tempers confidence in sustaining his effort over 1m3½f.

runners_data.name: Joanna Hiffernan
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows has hit a decent vein with 2 from 10 in the last 14 days and Callum Rodriguez knows this mare; her hold-up style has produced a sim-going course placing and she drops back to familiar ground, though her recent form of 6-4 suggests she needs things to fall right rather than being an outright threat.

runners_data.name: Al Maslool
runners_data.note: William Haggas's consistent record (8/27 in 14 days) backs a horse returning just 6 days after his last run — quick turnaround form the Haggas yard often means a horse is in good heart; though his natural style is rear-to-mid closing, the lack of strong pace in this field means he is unlikely to get the truly searching gallop his best form has required.

runners_data.name: Argenteus
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's lightly raced 3yo is an unknown quantity on going and style, making form assessment very limited; the booking of the 7lb claimer Dominique Van Der Kraats suggests confidence may be modest, but Menuisier occasionally brings unexposed improvers who surprise in novice company.

runners_data.name: Cape Fear
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo has a solid consistent profile (2-3-2-3 in recent runs) and handles Good ground well; his true style is as a hold-up closer, and with the pace likely to be controlled rather than strong, he may find the test not sharp enough to enable his best late finish from his expected mid-group position.

runners_data.name: Moon Zabeel
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo is a complete unknown — no going preference established, style unknown, debutant-level data — though the trainer has been among the winners (5/45 in 14 days) and this longer trip may suit an unexposed stayer; must be treated as a wildcard.

runners_data.name: Golden Step
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's 3yo has placed in both her runs (3-3) at 11f including one on sim-going, giving her course relevance and a profile that suits this trip well; Josephine Gordon provides a competent pilot and the hold-up style may mean she is better placed than most to finish off a race run at this controlled pace.

races.paceDynamic: Garrincha is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no rival likely to press hard from the gates, he should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m3½f trip on Good ground at Lingfield. With Joanna Hiffernan, Al Maslool, Cape Fear, and Golden Step all natural hold-up or prominent types, the field congregates behind Garrincha rather than challenging his lead, meaning fractions are unlikely to be pressured and the pace will be honest but not punishing. The redistribution of Al Maslool and Cape Fear into midfield on the map is forced by the volume of hold-up horses — both are true closers who will likely find themselves in a mid-to-rear group unable to get the truly dawdling pace their style ideally requires. This shape — a single front-runner setting a measured tempo — most strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or in mid-division and produce a sustained gallop from two furlongs out, rather than those who need a truly searching pace to close from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Garrincha Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Garrincha bowls along at a fair but unchallenged pace and horses tracking him from second or third can sustain their effort into the straight.
scenarios.body: If Garrincha bowls along at a fair but unchallenged pace and horses tracking him from second or third can sustain their effort into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Garrincha Unchallenged Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up runners fail to quicken and Garrincha is allowed to coast home with no serious pursuit materialising.
scenarios.body: If the hold-up runners fail to quicken and Garrincha is allowed to coast home with no serious pursuit materialising.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Find Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the race evolves unusually slowly and hold-up horses get a dramatic late run.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses or the race evolves unusually slowly and hold-up horses get a dramatic late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improvers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Argenteus or Moon Zabeel, both unknown quantities with lightly raced profiles, show significant unexposed ability and outclass this novice field.
scenarios.body: If Argenteus or Moon Zabeel, both unknown quantities with lightly raced profiles, show significant unexposed ability and outclass this novice field.

watchPoints.text: Garrincha's 168-day absence is the single biggest risk factor — if he shows signs of greenness or weakness in the closing stages after setting his own pace, the race opens up entirely for the chasers.

Cape Fear and Al Maslool are both mapped to midfield rather than their true closing positions — watch whether they can actually obtain a forward enough berth to matter, or whether they drift back and make their task harder.

Golden Step's consistent placed record at this trip and similar going makes her the most likely beneficiary if Garrincha tires; watch her position turning for home as an indicator of whether the pace has been sufficient to wind up her finish.

Argenteus and Moon Zabeel are both unknown quantities — any significant market moves before the off for either lightly raced runner should be noted as potentially meaningful given the absence of public form to assess.

races.name: Free Tips At chracingclub.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Naasma
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has the lead role to herself here; Pat Phelan's yard is out of form (0/4 in 14 days) and 85 days off the track is a flag, but she won on this surface/distance combination and goes well fresh — the key question is whether she has enough left to last home over 2m½f after controlling the race.

runners_data.name: Love Is Golden
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Soft and Good going and was placed at the trip, so the distance holds no fears; Jack Dace (5lb claim) is an asset at the weights, though her single similar-going form line shows no wins or places from that sample — returns quickly on 13 days and the hood (headgear noted) may sharpen her.

runners_data.name: Kitty Foyle
runners_data.note: Boasts two wins and a place in her last five at distances between 16f and 25f on Good ground, making her the most proven stayer in the field over this sort of trip; Millie Wonnacott (5lb) keeps costs down, but 298 days off the track (30 days since a jumps run) is the one clear concern for a six-year-old needing to fire cold.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted and in good recent heart with a win and a place in his last two runs, both on Standard or Good; Jack Jones's yard is cold (0/12 in 14 days) and this step up from 16f to 20f is untested, but he is naturally prominent, should track Naasma comfortably, and has the profile to grind on if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Diamond Bay
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with genuine hold-up instincts who wears a hood and has course experience; the trainer lands a blow (1/10 in 14 days), but his last five runs show just two places and none over today's trip — his true nature as a hold-up runner means he needs a proper pace to hunt, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations about him benefiting from his mapped midfield slot.

runners_data.name: Rogue Empire
runners_data.note: Arrives on the back of back-to-back wins over 16f on Standard and Good, both at this trip range, making him the form pick on raw figures; a natural front-runner by instinct, he is bumped to a midfield draw by the crowded pace map and Owen Lewis (5lb) will need to adapt his tactics — the ability is there but his preferred position is compromised in this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Naasma is the one confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with only An Bradan Feasa as a natural prominent companion, she is virtually guaranteed an uncontested lead over 2m½f on Good ground at Lingfield. The pace will be steady but genuine enough at this trip — Naasma can dictate her own rhythm without being harassed, which at a flat, galloping track over this distance is a significant advantage. Rogue Empire is a genuine prominent type who will want to press forward but, with Naasma already holding that role and An Bradan Feasa also looking to track, the field holds more pace-hungry horses than the shape can comfortably accommodate, meaning Rogue Empire is likely to be pushed further back than ideal. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested lead at an honest but not frantic gallop — strongly favours hold-up horses who can travel smoothly off the pace and produce a sustained finish, particularly those with proven form at the trip and on Good turf.

watchPoints.text: Kitty Foyle's 298-day absence (most recent run was a hurdles start 30 days ago) is the biggest single fitness risk in the race — watch for any signs of sluggishness in the early stages over this stamina-sapping 2m½f trip.

Rogue Empire's natural desire to be prominent will create early tension; watch whether Owen Lewis attempts to push forward and crowd Naasma's lead or settles mid-pack — the outcome of that decision will shape who wins.

Love Is Golden's similar-going form record (1 run, 0 wins, 0 places) is remarkably thin for a horse whose price may reflect her course-and-distance win — treat that sample-size with caution before assuming she handles this precisely.

An Bradan Feasa steps up markedly in trip from 16f to 20f for the first time; if the pace stays controlled and he tracks Naasma as expected, watch whether he quickens or simply outstays rivals in the final two furlongs.
Diamond Bay's hood and the trainer's recent 1/10 strike rate is a minor positive angle — watch for an each-way move in the market as a signal that the yard believes conditions suit today.

races.name: Chris Haines Tips At Lingfield Handicap

runners_data.name: Ken Brulee
runners_data.note: Rated 55 and the highest-rated runner in the field, trained by Mark Usher and 13 days since last run, but holds a hold-up style that is entirely unsuited to this pace vacuum; similar-going form of 0W0P over 5f-6f at Standard is a concern, though Rose Dawes claiming 5lbs does soften the weight burden at 135lbs.

runners_data.name: Bridget's Baby
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's yard is firing at 10/59 over 14 days which is a workmanlike strike rate at best; a natural hold-up operator who has been placed in midfield only because the map is saturated with closers, meaning her chance depends heavily on her ability to quicken from a position she is unlikely to naturally occupy — the 7-lb claimer Myla Coppins is an added unknown.

runners_data.name: Kodi K
runners_data.note: Absent for 55 days and without a win or place in three runs over 6f on Good, Soft and Heavy, Kodi K faces the sharpest fitness query in this field; John Gallagher's yard has struck at 0/5 in the 14-day window, and the step down to 5f is unproven, making this runner the most speculative profile in the race despite sharing the same hold-up style as the rest.

runners_data.name: Lesley Buckley
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is an ominous tag in a race that is likely to be decided by a late sprint, and the headgear (blinkers) suggests connections are attempting to address that tendency; a true hold-up type pushed onto the map's midfield zone, her five-run history shows finishes of 7th, 8th, 10th, 9th and 11th — none over the 5f trip — and 23 days since last run is manageable but form gives little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: With all four runners carrying a hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner in this 5f sprint at Lingfield, this race faces a genuine pace vacuum from the gates — nobody wants to lead, which paradoxically means the early gallop could be slow and the race compressed into a furlong-long dash for the line. Bridget's Baby and Lesley Buckley are both true hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the field has more closers than it can accommodate at the rear, meaning neither is likely to secure even a midfield position naturally. Ken Brulee and Kodi K share the same reluctant-leader dynamic, leaving the shape entirely dependent on who blinks first and accepts an uncharacteristic position near the front under jockey pressure. In this scenario, the race favours whoever can produce the sharpest, most sustained finish from a compressed field — positional flexibility and raw speed over the final furlong matter most, making hold-up types who can quicken from a central position the primary beneficiaries, though the pace vacuum means any runner forced to lead against type will be placed under immediate pressure.

scenarios.body: If the field drifts into a dawdling early pace with all runners grouped and the race becomes a flat-out dash over the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Ken Brulee holds the highest OR (55) in a race where no horse naturally wants to lead — watch whether Rose Dawes attempts to push him forward from the gates, as any horse forced to front-run in this vacuum immediately becomes the one to beat.

Kodi K's 55-day absence in a 4-runner sprint is a significant risk factor — watch the market for any drift that signals stable confidence is lukewarm, as a flat-track field this small will expose any fitness shortfall immediately.

Lesley Buckley is flagged as fading in the finish and is wearing blinkers, suggesting a behavioural tendency that has already been identified by connections — watch her early in the race for signs of reluctance or erratic jumping, which in a 5f sprint could end her chance within the first furlong.

With all four runners sharing a hold-up profile, watch the draw and early positioning carefully at the start — whichever runner secures the best central berth and avoids being caught widest into the first bend will have a significant positional advantage in what is likely to become a bunched sprint.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Heddon Street
runners_data.note: Progressive filly with back-to-back wins at 6f on Good, natural front-runner under Callum Rodriguez for Michael Bell (4/25 T14 form); the uncontested lead is hers for the taking and she is at her most dangerous when allowed to dictate, though any horse that tracks her closely in a sustainable rhythm poses the main threat.

runners_data.name: Ocean Force
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up horse with disappointing recent form (7-5-5) at longer trips, dropping back to 6f; Tom Queally takes the ride but the sim-going record shows no wins or places, and a bigger field of closers is not ideal company for a horse that needs daylight late.

runners_data.name: Muchacho
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old held up last time at 6f on Good, finishing fourth; trainer Hilal Kobeissi has no T14 runners, limiting form intel, and Dylan Hogan will need to find a path through what is likely to be a bunched finish if this horse is to threaten.

runners_data.name: Smooth Flight
runners_data.note: Unknown style on debut for Henry Candy (good record with 6f types), partnered by the experienced Nicola Currie; lightly raced flag means style is genuinely unclear, but if Candy has this horse ready to go first time and she has natural pace, the uncontested race shape is exactly the blank canvas a newcomer needs.

runners_data.name: Eveninginparis
runners_data.note: Debutant from Richard Hannon's powerful stable (7/50 T14), ridden by Alec Voikhansky; Hannon typically produces 6f two-year-olds well but this is a three-year-old first-timer — an unknown quantity, though the yard's experience means tactical instructions will be sound.

runners_data.name: Mariselle
runners_data.note: Another debut runner, saddled by jockey-turned-trainer Adam Kirby (Pat Cosgrave in the irons); low T14 numbers offer little confidence from a form angle, and with style entirely unknown, she is the biggest wildcard in the race.

runners_data.name: Moravian
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for Gary & Josh Moore whose map position shows midfield only because rear slots were over-subscribed; form of 7-11 suggests struggles in this grade at 6-7f, and being repositioned forward of his natural comfort zone will compound the challenge — George Bass will need to manage this carefully.

runners_data.name: Rumble Ruby
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Lemos De Souza with a third at 6f on Standard in her best run (2/2 sim-going with one place); George Wood partners and she has the most relevant surface experience of the closers, but she needs gaps to open quickly in a race where the hold-up contingent is large.

runners_data.name: Cortado Girl
runners_data.note: Returning from a 287-day absence for Hayley Turner's small operation and a natural hold-up filly who fades in the finish — her redistribution to midfield on the map reflects traffic realities rather than ability to race there; the long lay-off, fade flag, and race-rusty status combine to make her a significant risk.

races.paceDynamic: Heddon Street is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this 6f novice, and with no genuine challenger willing or able to press for the lead, she should cruise into an uncontested position at the head of affairs and control tempo entirely on her own terms. The remainder of the field — Ocean Force, Muchacho, Rumble Ruby, and the lightly-raced debutants — are all hold-up or unknown types who will be content to track or close from behind, meaning there is no credible threat to Heddon Street's ability to dictate. Moravian and Cortado Girl are true hold-up horses pushed into the midfield map position because the rear of the field is congested with closers, and neither should be expected to race prominently despite that placement. The resulting shape is a controlled, honest pace set by one horse — a scenario that almost exclusively favours prominent racers who can track the leader in a smooth rhythm and quicken in the straight, with genuine hold-up horses facing the challenge of finding daylight late through a field that will not string out enough to create gaps.

watchPoints.text: Heddon Street's early position is critical — if she misses the break or is pushed wide, the entire race shape dissolves and hold-up horses gain an unlikely advantage they would not otherwise have.

Moravian and Cortado Girl are genuine closers mapped to midfield due to congestion — watch whether they settle further back than their map position implies, leaving them with ground to make up they cannot cover in 6f.

Smooth Flight and Eveninginparis are debut runners with no observable style — if either shows natural speed and positions prominently, they immediately become live factors that the pace map could not anticipate.

Rumble Ruby has the strongest sim-going credentials of all the hold-up horses — if she gets a clean run from midfield in the final 2f, she is the most capable closer at this track and surface combination.

Field of nine over Lingfield 6f on Good ground tends to produce a compacted finish if pace is solo and controlled — watch for a bunching effect rounding the home turn that could trap hold-up horses and hand the advantage entirely to Heddon Street and any close trailer.

races.name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Apple's Angel
runners_data.note: Trainer Jim Boyle quiet of late (0/11 in 14 days), last ran 20 days ago, and her sim-going form at Lingfield is modest (9th of 15 comparable runs); a natural hold-up horse who will race toward the rear, which is a problematic profile in a race likely to be decided by position.|

runners_data.name: Charging Bull
runners_data.note: Holds a decent recent placed effort at 5f on Standard going and returns after just 7 days, suggesting trainer Keady is happy with the horse; runs with tongue-tie and will try to close from behind, though in a muddling field with no true pace this hold-up style is less effective than it sounds on paper.|

runners_data.name: Comedian Leader
runners_data.note: 90-day absence is the standout concern here — Jim & Suzi Best have been in form (2/4 in 14 days) but a horse returning from three months off over a sprint distance faces a fitness question that is hard to overcome; drops back to hold-up position but has no sim-going wins or placed efforts to underpin confidence.|

runners_data.name: Dios De La Guerra
runners_data.note: Simon Dow sends this one out 17 days after its last run with a worrying finishing pattern — flagged as fading in the finish and has run 11th and 11th in recent similar-going outings; a hold-up horse who appears to stop when it matters most, which is a critical negative in a race that will already have a slow tempo.|

runners_data.name: Dr Ali
runners_data.note: Has two wins and five places across 14 recent sim-going outings (14/15), making him the most exposed but also most reliable in this type of race; hg:p tag suggests prominent headgear encourages a forward-going approach, which could be a decisive advantage if his rider commits to the front in a field with no confirmed pace-setter.|

runners_data.name: Lion Ring
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with two wins in 13 sim-going outings and placed five times, indicating experience of exactly this type of race; his natural hold-up style is pushed forward by redistribution — the key question is whether his jockey Ryan Kavanagh (claiming 5lbs) can get the gelding into a useful early position.|

runners_data.name: Little Miss Magic
runners_data.note: Visors noted in her profile and she has run 5th, 7th, 6th, 7th, 7th in her last five — relentlessly consistent in finishing midfield without ever threatening to win; her 8/15 sim-going strike rate for places doesn't translate to competitive runs in a sprint finish where position is everything.|

runners_data.name: Top Biller
runners_data.note: Had a placed effort (2nd) on Good ground at 6f at Lingfield in recent form, which is the most directly relevant piece of course-and-distance form in this field; trainer Birkett has one winner in eight 14-day runners — Top Biller's natural rear-running style means it must find a clean passage, and hg:tb (tongue-tie/blinkers combination) hints at concentration issues that make that harder.|

runners_data.name: Voodoo Ray
runners_data.note: Tom Queally — a high-class jockey — partners this seven-year-old for Gary & Josh Moore (4/31 in 14 days, active stable); sim-going form is weak (5/15, no wins or places) and the horse's last win is buried in its history — the jockey booking is the main reason to take a second look rather than any recent form evidence.|

runners_data.name: Magnificent Mel
runners_data.note: A three-year-old carrying a lower weight (128lbs) compared to the older horses on 135lbs — that allowance is a tangible edge in a race decided by the narrowest of margins; two placed efforts on Good ground at 6f in recent outings (2/6f/GOO and 2/5f/GOO) make her the most consistently placed runner in conditions closest to tonight's.|

runners_data.name: Tass
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's three-year-old has run just three times in recorded history here, returning after 46 days off — the layoff and limited form base make her the most unknown quantity in the field; on 128lbs like Magnificent Mel and with a Nicola Currie booking for a trainer who has one winner in eleven recent runners, she needs to improve significantly on what she has shown.

races.paceDynamic: This is a field of eleven that is almost entirely composed of hold-up horses, with no confirmed front-runner emerging from the data — the race is likely to produce a slow-burn, messy contest that collapses into a sprint finish from around two furlongs out. With every runner carrying a hold-up style profile, no horse is expected to seize the initiative early, meaning the pace will be manufactured by default rather than design, likely resulting in a falsely-run affair over six furlongs on Good-standard Lingfield turf. Dr Ali, Lion Ring, Top Biller, Magnificent Mel, Apple's Angel and Charging Bull are all redistributed to midfield on the map but are true hold-up types; none are natural front-runners and so the early gallop will be fragile, handing an edge to whoever is sharpest out of the gates on the day. The tactical verdict is clear: with no true pace-setter and a field that will bunch and sprint, horses who can find a good early position without burning energy, travel close to the pace by default, and produce a sharp late effort in the final furlong — a profile akin to a prominent-to-midfield runner in a muddling race — are best placed, while genuine closers who need a true gallop to set up their run are at the mercy of an uncooperative shape.

watchPoints.text: Dr Ali is the horse to watch for early position — if Taylor Fisher pushes forward from the gate using the hg:p to its maximum effect in a field with no willing front-runner, Dr Ali could steal an uncontested lead that would be very difficult to peg back in a muddling contest.

Dios De La Guerra is flagged as fading in finishes and has posted two last-place results in recent similar-going outings — watch whether Simon Dow's runner is competitive at all, as a horse with a stopping pattern in a sprint finish is a significant betting and race-shape risk.

Magnificent Mel's 5lb weight-for-age allowance over the older horses could be decisive in a tight finish — watch her market position as race time approaches; if punters are on to this angle the market will shorten, confirming the advantage is being priced in.

With a 90-day break, Comedian Leader (Jim & Suzi Best) should be monitored in the paddock and at the start — a fresh horse in a sprint can sometimes show more than expected first time back, but the stable's 2/4 14-day record suggests horses are ready when sent, making an eye-catching run possible even if the form book looks bleak.

Tom Queally's presence on Voodoo Ray for the Moore yard is worth tracking — Moore's are a busy operation (4/31 in 14 days) and a jockey of Queally's calibre rarely accepts a 7-year-old with weak sim-going form without reason; watch for any significant gamble or stable confidence indicators pre-race.
